response.query: How should we formally define and annotate hallucination rate across multi-step agent outputs, including gold-label schema, aggregation rules, and automated heuristics to validate at scale?
response.answer: Hallucination rate in multi-step agent outputs is defined as the proportion of incorrect or irrelevant information generated. Gold-label schema uses human-annotated data for validation. Automated heuristics include statistical measures and cross-validation techniques for large-scale validation.

results.content: Yuwei Zhao | Ziyang Luo | Yuchen Tian | Hongzhan Lin | Weixiang Yan | Annan Li | Jing Ma. Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) have showcased impressive code generation capabilities, primarily evaluated through language-to-code benchmarks. In this paper, we explore alternative way of leveraging Large Language Model (LLM) generated feedback to address the inherent limitation of using human-labeled data. Recent research in federated large language models (LLMs) has primarily focused on enabling clients to fine-tune their locally deployed homogeneous LLMs collaboratively or on transferring knowledge from server-based LLMs to small language models (SLMs) at downstream clients. Our analysis demonstrates that this task is highly challenging, with large language models (LLMs) yielding unsatisfactory performance. In this paper, we propose a data augmentation method via lightweight large language model (LLM) generation and tree hybridization.
